content: 1. Clarithromycin affects the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug in such cases. 2. Clarithromycin significantly increases the effects of bemiparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and therapy may need to be modified. 4. Co-administration of clarithromycin with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can elevate hydrocodone plasma concentrations (benzhydrocodone is a prodrug of hydrocodone), potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring is essential. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. If co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor, reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Bexarotene decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bivalirudin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 13. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor or of unknown significance. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If the dose of the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients transferring from transmucosal buprenorphine co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors to ensure adequate plasma levels. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buspirone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by increasing its elimination via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by increasing its elimination via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabergoline by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 32. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations should be closely monitored. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefoxitin, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Chlorpromazine and clarithromycin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin decreases the efficacy of the cholera vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics. 46. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by decreasing its elimination. Avoid inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP). 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Clarithromycin and cisapride both increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 54. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of citalopram by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
